Florida Statutes, section 605.0213 - Fees of the department (LLC)

amount.note: The Division of Corporations lists a $100 filing fee (required) for a new Florida LLC, the same amount set in Florida Statutes section 605.0213.

sources.title: Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations - LLC Fees

amount.note: The Division of Corporations lists this $25 fee as required for a new Florida LLC, for a total of $125 with the filing fee.

annual.label: Annual report fee
annual.due: Delivered between January 1 and May 1 each year, first in the year after the LLC is formed. Received after May 1, the Division lists $538.75 instead.

sources.title: Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations - LLC Fees
Florida Statutes, section 605.0212 - Annual report for department (LLC)

amount.note: The Division of Corporations lists the annual report (and supplemental fee) at $138.75. The statute sets when the report is due: first in the year after formation.

notIncluded.label: Late fee for a missed annual report
notIncluded.reason: Not a cost every LLC pays. The Division lists the annual report at $538.75 when received after May 1, instead of $138.75. The statute says an LLC that does not file can be dissolved and cannot bring or defend a lawsuit in Florida courts until it files.

notIncluded.label: Registered agent service
notIncluded.reason: Only if you hire a registered agent. The agent sets the price, so it is not a state fee and is not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Name reservation
notIncluded.reason: Optional. Reserving a name before you file is a separate charge and is not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Local business licenses and permits
notIncluded.reason: City, county and industry licenses depend on where the business operates and what it does. None are in the total.

notIncluded.label: Federal and state income taxes
notIncluded.reason: Taxes on the LLC's or its owners' income are not part of this estimate. This page is not legal or tax advice.

notIncluded.label: Expedited filing
notIncluded.reason: Optional. Faster processing costs extra and is not in the total.

content.intro: {state} charges a filing fee and a required registered agent fee to form an LLC, then an annual report fee each year after that. A report filed after the early-May deadline costs much more.

howItWorks.text: The Division of Corporations charges a filing fee and a required registered agent fee when you form a new LLC. The fees are also set in {state} law.
The annual report must be delivered within a set window early each year, starting in the year after the LLC is formed. Filed after the deadline, the report costs much more.
An LLC that does not file the annual report can be dissolved, and it may not bring or defend a lawsuit in {state} courts until the report is filed and the fees and penalties are paid.

faq.q: Is the registered agent fee required in {state}?
faq.text: Yes. The Division of Corporations lists it as required for every new LLC, on top of the filing fee. It is a state fee, separate from what a paid registered agent service would charge.

faq.q: When is the annual report due for a {state} LLC?
faq.text: It is delivered within a window early each year, and the first one falls in the year after the LLC is formed.

faq.q: What happens if a {state} LLC misses the annual report?
faq.text: It can be dissolved, and until it files and pays the fees and penalties it may not bring or defend a lawsuit in {state} courts.
